unit-1.title: What Scientists Mean by Matter
unit-1.description: Define matter as anything that has mass and takes up space; separate matter from energy and ideas.

unit-1.title: States of Matter: Solid, Liquid, Gas
unit-1.description: Compare solids, liquids, and gases by shape, volume, and particle motion.

unit-1.title: Particle Model Thinking
unit-1.description: Use a simple particle model to explain freezing, melting, and evaporation.

unit-1.title: Measuring Mass and Volume
unit-1.description: Measure mass and volume carefully; choose tools that match the sample.

unit-1.title: Density as a Physical Property
unit-1.description: Compute and compare density; predict float/sink relative to a fluid.

unit-1.title: Pure Substances vs Mixtures
unit-1.description: Distinguish pure substances from homogeneous and heterogeneous mixtures.

unit-1.title: Physical Properties Lab Habits
unit-1.description: Plan fair tests of physical properties: control variables and record units.

unit-1.title: Physical Changes Around Us
unit-1.description: Identify physical changes that rearrange matter without making a new substance.

unit-1.title: Matter Unit Synthesis
unit-1.description: Connect particle ideas, density, and mixtures in one evidence-based explanation.

unit-2.title: Elements as Building Blocks
unit-2.description: Explain that elements are pure substances made of one kind of atom.

unit-2.title: Reading the Periodic Table
unit-2.description: Locate metals, nonmetals, and metalloids and describe shared physical properties.

unit-2.title: Metals, Nonmetals, and Metalloids
unit-2.description: Compare conductivity, luster, and malleability across element classes.

unit-2.title: Compounds vs Elements
unit-2.description: Distinguish compounds from elements using composition language.

unit-2.title: Evidence of Chemical Change
unit-2.description: List evidence (gas, color, temperature, precipitate) that a new substance may form.

unit-2.title: Physical vs Chemical Change Sort
unit-2.description: Classify everyday changes and justify with evidence, not slogans.

unit-2.title: Conservation of Mass Intro
unit-2.description: Argue that mass is conserved in closed-system chemical changes at intro level.

unit-2.title: Chemical Changes Unit Review
unit-2.description: Synthesize element identity, compounds, and chemical-change evidence.

unit-3.title: What Is a Force?
unit-3.description: Define force as a push or pull; measure force conceptually in newtons.

unit-3.title: Contact and Noncontact Forces
unit-3.description: Classify gravity, friction, magnetism, applied, and normal forces.

unit-3.title: Gravity Near Earth
unit-3.description: Describe gravity as an attractive force toward Earth’s center; connect to weight.

unit-3.title: Friction Helps and Hinders
unit-3.description: Explain how friction can start, stop, or slow motion depending on the situation.

unit-3.title: Magnetism Basics
unit-3.description: Describe magnetic poles and attraction/repulsion without treating magnets as magic.

unit-3.title: Balanced and Unbalanced Forces
unit-3.description: Decide whether forces are balanced; predict constant motion vs acceleration.

unit-3.title: Net Force on a Line
unit-3.description: Calculate simple one-dimensional net force from force diagrams.

unit-3.title: Action–Reaction Pairs Intro
unit-3.description: Identify force pairs that are equal and opposite on interacting objects.

unit-3.title: Forces Unit Synthesis
unit-3.description: Explain a real motion story using force types, net force, and evidence.

unit-4.title: Energy as the Ability to Cause Change
unit-4.description: Define energy and distinguish forms without inventing energy from nowhere.

unit-4.title: Kinetic Energy
unit-4.description: Relate kinetic energy to mass and speed qualitatively.

unit-4.title: Gravitational Potential Energy
unit-4.description: Relate GPE to height and mass in everyday contexts.

unit-4.title: Elastic and Chemical Potential Energy
unit-4.description: Identify stored energy in springs, rubber bands, food, and fuels at intro level.

unit-4.title: Energy Transfers and Transformations
unit-4.description: Track energy as it transfers between objects or transforms between forms.

unit-4.title: Conservation of Energy Habit
unit-4.description: Use conservation language: energy changes form; totals stay accountable in a system.

unit-4.title: Waves Transfer Energy
unit-4.description: Describe waves as energy movers that do not permanently transport the medium.

unit-4.title: Energy Unit Review
unit-4.description: Mixed practice connecting KE, PE, transfers, and conservation language.

unit-5.title: Earth’s Place in the Solar System
unit-5.description: Locate Earth among the Sun and planets; scale ideas with humility about distances.

unit-5.title: Day and Night
unit-5.description: Explain day/night using Earth’s rotation — not the Sun “going away.”

unit-5.title: Seasons and Tilt
unit-5.description: Connect seasons to Earth’s tilt and orbit, not to distance-from-Sun myths.

unit-5.title: Moon Phases from Earth
unit-5.description: Predict moon phase patterns from relative positions of Earth, Moon, and Sun.

unit-5.title: Solar and Lunar Eclipses
unit-5.description: Model why eclipses are rare using shadow geometry.

unit-5.title: Tides Intro
unit-5.description: Connect tidal patterns to the Moon’s gravitational influence at an intro level.

unit-5.title: Scale Models and Limits
unit-5.description: Critique classroom models: what they show well and what they distort.

unit-5.title: Earth-Sun-Moon Unit Synthesis
unit-5.description: Explain one phenomenon (season, phase, or eclipse) with a labeled model + CER.

unit-6.title: Earth’s Spheres Overview
unit-6.description: Name geosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere, and biosphere and give one interaction.

unit-6.title: Layers of Earth (Intro)
unit-6.description: Describe crust, mantle, and core at a Grade 6 model level.

unit-6.title: Rocks and the Rock Cycle
unit-6.description: Connect igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks through processes.

unit-6.title: Plate Tectonics Basics
unit-6.description: Explain that plates move slowly and cause earthquakes, volcanoes, and mountain building.

unit-6.title: Texas Geology Hooks
unit-6.description: Connect East Texas landscapes to sedimentary history and resources without oversimplifying.

unit-6.title: Weathering, Erosion, Deposition
unit-6.description: Distinguish weathering from erosion and deposition with local examples.

unit-6.title: Water Cycle as a System
unit-6.description: Trace water through evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and runoff.

unit-6.title: Earth Systems Unit Review
unit-6.description: Explain a change (flood, landslide, or rock formation) across multiple spheres.

unit-7.title: Natural Resources Inventory
unit-7.description: Classify renewable and nonrenewable resources with Texas-relevant examples.

unit-7.title: Energy Resources Tradeoffs
unit-7.description: Compare resource options using evidence about availability, impact, and cost — not slogans.

unit-7.title: Water as a Precious Resource
unit-7.description: Explain why freshwater management matters in Texas climates.

unit-7.title: Soil and Land Use
unit-7.description: Connect soil health to farming, runoff, and erosion control.

unit-7.title: Human Impact Evidence
unit-7.description: Use data (not vibes) to describe how human activity can help or harm systems.

unit-7.title: Conservation and Stewardship Habits
unit-7.description: Propose practical stewardship actions tied to science explanations.

unit-7.title: Resources Unit Synthesis
unit-7.description: Argue for one management choice using claims, evidence, and tradeoffs.

unit-8.title: Ecosystem Components
unit-8.description: Distinguish biotic and abiotic factors in a local ecosystem model.

unit-8.title: Habitats and Niches
unit-8.description: Explain habitat vs niche with concrete organism examples.

unit-8.title: Food Chains and Food Webs
unit-8.description: Trace energy flow; prefer webs over single chains for realism.

unit-8.title: Producers, Consumers, Decomposers
unit-8.description: Classify roles and explain why decomposers matter.

unit-8.title: Competition and Predation
unit-8.description: Describe interactions that shape populations without moralizing animals.

unit-8.title: Symbiosis Intro
unit-8.description: Identify mutualism, commensalism, and parasitism with evidence.

unit-8.title: Ecosystem Changes and Stability
unit-8.description: Predict how removing a key species or resource can ripple through a web.

unit-8.title: Ecosystems Unit Review
unit-8.description: Build a mini food web and justify two interaction claims with evidence.

unit-9.title: Cells as Building Blocks
unit-9.description: Argue that living things are made of cells; connect structure to function at intro level.

unit-9.title: Plant vs Animal Cells
unit-9.description: Compare key organelles students can map on diagrams (cell wall, chloroplast, etc.).

unit-9.title: Microscope Habits
unit-9.description: Practice responsible observation: focus, scale, and honest drawings.

unit-9.title: Unicellular and Multicellular Life
unit-9.description: Contrast single-celled organisms with multicellular organization.

unit-9.title: Organization: Cells to Systems
unit-9.description: Sequence cells → tissues → organs → systems with a human or plant example.

unit-9.title: Photosynthesis Overview
unit-9.description: Explain that plants capture light energy to make sugars; write inputs/outputs carefully.

unit-9.title: Human Body Systems Intro
unit-9.description: Map how two systems work together (e.g., respiratory + circulatory).

unit-9.title: Cells & Organisms Unit Synthesis
unit-9.description: Use a diagram + CER to connect cell structures to organism needs.

unit-10.title: Traits We Can Observe
unit-10.description: Distinguish inherited traits from learned behaviors and environmental effects.

unit-10.title: Variation Within a Species
unit-10.description: Explain why variation matters for survival in changing conditions.

unit-10.title: Genes as Instructions (Intro)
unit-10.description: Introduce genes as inherited instructions without overclaiming DNA detail.

unit-10.title: Environment Shapes Expression
unit-10.description: Give examples where environment influences how traits appear (height nutrition, etc.).

unit-10.title: Adaptations Are Not Wishes
unit-10.description: Define adaptations as heritable traits that help survival/reproduction in a habitat.

unit-10.title: Selective Pressures Stories
unit-10.description: Reason about how conditions can favor certain variations over generations (intro).

unit-10.title: Traits Unit Review
unit-10.description: Sort claim types: inherited, environmental, both — with evidence.

unit-10.title: Year Capstone: Systems Thinking
unit-10.description: Connect matter/energy, Earth systems, ecosystems, and traits in one stewardship CER.
